oliver: Quick heads-up — ran a focused microbenchmark on Ampere64 with the new kernel selector tweaks. Seeing a consistent p50 regression on the prefill path for short contexts (<64 tokens), decode path looks unchanged. dump attached (summary below).

maya: can you paste the numbers?

oliver: sure, pasted snippet:```
model: rw-13b-raw
batch: 32
seq: 48 (prefill)
old-selector p50: 12.1ms
new-selector p50: 18.6ms  <-- regressed
old-selector p95: 63ms
new-selector p95: 86ms
decode (seq=1) old p50: 10.8ms new p50: 11.2ms
KV hit rate during prefill: 0.0 -> full KV write pressure
mem_bw observed increase ~14%
profiling: kernel_pick_trace: candidate_set=[matmul_fused_v1, matmul_wmma_int8, matmul_smallseq_fp16], picked=matmul_fused_v1, reason=cost_estimate_latency
```

srujan: interesting. matmul_fused_v1 historically wins for mid/long sequences but not for tiny seqs. Looks like the cost model's sequence-length term got scaled up. do you have the autotune logs?

oliver: attached autotune snapshot. The cost function is now using tokens_per_sec_estimate := op_time / (seq_norm + eps) and seq_norm seems to be higher for short seq due to the new warmup penalty.

maya: warmup penalty? we added that to avoid tiny-sample noise. Might be too aggressive.

oliver: exactly. For prefill we also have KV writes which increase memory pressure — that shifts the latency profile such that the fused kernel becomes worse in practice because it hits L2 bandwidth more. The estimator didn't include a KV_active term.

tess: i can repro locally on a small harness. dump of kernel picks per request:```
[ts=3129876544] seq=48 batch=32 kv_active=true -> pick matmul_fused_v1 (est 15ms, actual 19ms)
[ts=3129876545] seq=8  batch=32 kv_active=false -> pick matmul_smallseq_fp16 (est 6ms, actual 6.2ms)
[ts=3129876546] seq=48 batch=32 kv_active=false -> pick matmul_wmma_int8 (est 14ms, actual 14.1ms)
```

srujan: that trace is gold. Suggestion: add kv_active boolean to the cost model and reduce warmup_penalty factor for seq<64. Also experiment with lowering the sequence_bucket_stride to avoid lumping 48 and 64 together.

maya: +1. concrete actions: (1) add kv_active to estimator, (2) add small-seq override: if seq<=64 && batch>=16 prefer smallseq kernel unless mem_bw_exceed threshold, (3) run autotune sweep with seq_bucket_stride=8 and collect p50/p95.

oliver: i pushed a quick patch prototype that exposes kernel_pick_reason and seq_bin in traces. PR here: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/5483 (wip)

perf-bot: scheduled autotune job #3129 for branch oliver/prefill-kernel-guard (ETA ~43m) :rocket:

tess: i'll add the mem_bw_exceed check — we can compute an instantaneous mem_bw estimate from nvprof counters and flip to int8 path when above threshold. keep in mind int8 path has higher kernel launch overhead for small batches.

srujan: beware oscillation: if we flip based on instantaneous mem_bw we might thrash between kernels on bursty KV writes. add hysteresis: require sustained mem_bw>thr for 3 consecutive windows.

maya: agree. also plan a 5% canary in eu-west-1 once autotune job finishes and we're happy with metrics.

oliver: thanks — prioritized: add kv flag to estimator, lower warmup_penalty for seq<64, add hysteresis window for mem_bw gating, enable richer logging. i'll follow up with a short postmortem if regressed numbers don't improve. :thumbsup:
